narrative:
The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 29.0%. Although that is not a certainty of default, it was above the lender’s risk cutoff for this loan, so the application was denied.

The most influential factor was your checking account status: you have no checking account recorded, which is common among approved applicants and worked in your favour. The second most important factor was an existing installment plan at a bank. This was the clearest risk-raising item among the top factors, because very few approved applicants have this type of plan. The third most important factor was the requested credit duration. At 12 months, it is shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, so this also worked slightly in your favour.

Overall, the denial reflects the combined risk profile rather than one isolated item. Your checking account status and shorter requested duration helped, but they were not enough to offset the risk signal from the existing bank installment plan and other less influential details in your profile.

Before reapplying, focus on reducing or clearing the existing bank installment obligation, strengthening your banking relationship, and keeping employment and residence information stable and up to date. Ask the lender whether a guarantor or co-applicant would be considered, and avoid submitting multiple new applications until your existing debt commitments are lower.
